answer: A verifiable delay protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to maintain an unbroken cryptographic thread verified at an ingress jetty. Participants prove liveness by solving sequential, non-parallelizable mathematical challenges. Because an attacker cannot forge these temporal outputs without dedicating real-time processor cycles per identity, scaling fake nodes imposes linear compute costs. However, this defense wastes substantial energy and favors adversaries with faster custom ASICs.
